fact_text: An ETF can only deliver the return of whatever it holds, so its usefulness depends entirely on the quality of its constituents rather than on the wrapper itself.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A thinly traded Pakistani ETF may show no price fall on a sharp market down day simply because there is no buyer to transact against, so its quoted price is not evidence of resilience.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan lacks a true index ETF; the handful that exist hold only about 10-12 companies, so they merely approximate the KSE-100 rather than replicating it, and deviations are expected.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: For a small portfolio the analyst favours simply matching index weights, because a 10% outperformance on a one-to-two million rupee portfolio adds little in absolute terms relative to the research time it consumes.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Measured from 1 January 1999, the Pakistani equity index compounded roughly 110 times, which the analyst presents as the benchmark for other local asset classes.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Over the same period starting 1 January 1999 gold rose roughly 50-55 times in rupee terms, about half the wealth creation the equity index delivered despite currency devaluation and a gold rally.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Bank savings and fixed-income products returned only about 10-12 times over the 25 years from 1999, against long-run average inflation of roughly 10% a year.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The US dollar rose only about five times against the rupee over the 25 years from 1999, moving from roughly 55 to 280, far less than local equity compounding.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Equities hedge rupee depreciation over the medium and long run because a company's long-term earning power is effectively dollar-denominated, but during the devaluation itself macro uncertainty dominates and prices lag.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's boom-and-bust framework is monitored monthly on three variables: the policy interest rate, the current account deficit, and the status of the IMF programme.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A roughly 10 dollar fall in the oil price lifts the Pakistani market's price-earnings multiple by about one point, which translates into something like a 15-20% valuation uplift across companies.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The central bank has been cutting rates slowly and cautiously on the logic that faster easing would push imports out of control, which is the main policy difference the analyst sees versus earlier easing cycles.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A falling interest-rate cycle is not monotonic: rates need not drop every month or even every quarter and can tick up briefly before resuming their decline.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A digital customs single-window system has importers' duty assessments approved by officers they cannot identify or contact, which is intended to curb under-invoicing and collusion on import duties.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Agricultural income tax has been enacted in law and efforts continue to bring retailers into the tax net, but the analyst notes collection from these measures has so far been small.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: While a government is inside an IMF programme the fiscal and current accounts are necessarily kept under control; the real test of reform only arrives when the programme ends or compliance slips.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: IMF money is typically not released before the federal budget because the budget fixes the coming year's fiscal numbers; in 2023 the budget was approved first and the staff-level agreement followed.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A budget tax aimed at one company or sector can be handled by shifting portfolio weights, but an increase in dividend or capital-gains tax hits every equity holder and cannot be positioned around.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: If structural reforms hold for two to three years the analyst expects a market-wide multiple rerating into double-digit P/Es, even where individual sectors such as banks see earnings growth slow as rates fall.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Two headline policy targets the analyst tracks are bringing the electricity tariff to about 9 US cents per unit and the policy interest rate to about 9%, with the tariff target seen as the harder of the two.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A share split leaves share capital unchanged while raising the share count and cutting per-share value, whereas a bonus issue capitalises reserves and so increases paid-up share capital.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Under the bonus-share tax, 10% of the shares issued in a bonus are withheld by the company to settle the tax, so the shareholder only receives the balance until the company releases the rest.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because a bonus issue draws down reserves while a split does not, companies that have issued bonus shares would be comparatively insulated if a tax on undistributed reserves were reintroduced.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst flags as unexplained the company's failure to release the additional 10% of bonus shares withheld for tax, suggesting the share price fall after the bonus left it short of the cash needed to settle the tax.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst attributes the company's long-run track record to three things he can monitor: two-tier gas pricing, rising production volumes, and the quality of its field.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The data-centre venture is immaterial to the company: an investment of roughly 10 billion rupees against a company worth several hundred billion, with the feasibility study implying only about 5-6 billion rupees of earnings over several years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst doubts Pakistan can scale data centres meaningfully because local electricity is not cheap enough by global standards to make the country a preferred hosting location.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Mining returns hinge on ore grade, the mining analogue of drilling depth and success ratio in oil and gas: how much earth must be moved for a gram of gold, with three to four grams per ton of ore counting as a tier-one mine.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Mine sites generally lack grid power, so trucks and machinery run on diesel or furnace oil, making fuel the dominant energy cost of a mining operation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argues Pakistani diesel carries a lower tax burden, at most around 70-100 rupees per litre, than in many other countries, which helps the economics of diesel-intensive activities such as mining.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Every business should ultimately be judged on return on invested capital: how much must be invested and what future profit that investment produces.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Asset-light does not imply high returns on capital: oil and gas drilling is very capital intensive yet earns good returns because of how its output pricing is set.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Once future profits are estimated correctly, only a high return on invested capital can justify a high price-earnings multiple; nothing else does.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The most reliable guide to the multiple a cyclical company can earn is the multiple it received in the previous cycle, nudged up by a point or two if the business has since grown in stature.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Before relying on a company's long-run track record the analyst writes down the three or four specific reasons behind it, so that a bad year can be judged against whether those drivers have actually changed.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst defines value investing broadly enough to include growth: the fair price is all the future value accruing to a shareholder, which embraces future projects, sponsor quality and even employee culture, not just a low P/E or P/B.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's listed universe is dominated by industrial complexes and physical assets whose value can be appraised directly, with few low-infrastructure, human-capital-driven businesses.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst builds positions in stages, locking in a small weight while a company is merely cheap and raising it as results and communication improve, which shortens the wait for value realisation versus sizing up at once.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A company's fair value rises simply with the passage of time as retained profits accumulate, so an unchanged share price becomes progressively cheaper even without any operational improvement.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Whether to use consolidated or unconsolidated accounts depends on which business you want to see, and the answer differs by company rather than following any general rule.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Consolidated accounts are the better lens for this cement producer because its captive power plant sits in a subsidiary yet is economically part of the same production complex.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: To look at the fertilizer business itself the analyst prefers unconsolidated accounts, because consolidation pulls in unrelated subsidiary activities.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The stock stayed cheap for a long stretch because the market read its investment in an affiliated hospital project as value destruction, management communicated the plan poorly, and a Punjab royalty was then imposed, leaving it without triggers.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because the company runs its own coal-fired captive power plant, electricity tariff relief packages matter less to it, while a fall in coal prices cuts both its fuel and its electricity cost.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst values cement capacity on an enterprise value per ton basis, noting the market has historically been willing to take Pakistani cement companies up to around 60 US dollars per ton of capacity.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The price-earnings ratio is a poor tool for cement because when per-bag profits spike the market knows the earnings are unsustainable and awards a low multiple; dollars of value per ton of capacity is the better frame.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The swing items in a cement producer's quarterly cost base are coal prices, electricity, distribution expenses that move with dispatch volumes, and finance cost which falls as interest rates decline.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Cement revenue is driven by retention price per bag together with dispatch volumes, so a fall in retention combined with softer volumes compresses revenue even when costs are falling.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In a results season the analyst ranks cement companies by how little their gross and operating margins contracted, treating the worst margin contractions as a signal the share will struggle until the next quarterly result.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Cement players had projected industry dispatches roughly double what actually materialised, so they generate surplus cash against unused capacity and are more likely than other sectors to diversify into unrelated businesses.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Cement sells for cash with no credit period, which gives the sector a better cash conversion cycle than glass, where two to three months of customer credit is normal.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Gas, largely imported LNG, is the critical cost input for flat glass, so the analyst tracks glass selling prices against the direction of gas cost; one listed player has contracted its gas supply with another company.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Only two listed glass companies are large and genuinely linked to the construction cycle; glass tubing and similar products belong to a different industry with different drivers.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst would award construction-linked glass a lower multiple than cement but better than steel: if these companies earned about a 5 times P/E last cycle, perhaps 6 times is reachable now, and he would not stretch beyond that.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The glass duopoly enjoys a price floor because competition is limited and imports are not a real threat, which makes its cyclicality milder than steel's.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A partnership with Lucky Cement has improved the market's perception of this glass maker, moving it closer to being seen as a tier-one company.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The asset management and currency exchange subsidiaries are consolidated into the bank's accounts but contribute at most a low single-digit share of profitability, so they can be ignored when analysing the bank.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst sees the bank's moat as brand: a customer who does not want an interest-bearing savings account turns to it first, which lets it grow deposits rapidly while keeping around half of them in current accounts.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The bank's savings return follows no fixed spread off the policy rate; the rule is that depositors receive about 75% of the average return earned on the bank's financing pool, which keeps it loosely linked to interest rates.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A conventional Pakistani bank's savings rate is formulaic, typically the policy rate less about 1.5 percentage points under the minimum deposit rate rule, which makes its deposit cost mechanically predictable.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Banks win current accounts by selling business convenience rather than return, for example granting traders far higher daily interbank transfer limits than rivals so they can transact after banking hours.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The bank has historically been able to pay materially less on savings deposits than rival Islamic banks and windows while still growing, which the analyst attributes to branding and customer selection rather than price competition.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argues the bank could do roughly four times its current volume of business without its economics changing much, making the model unusually scalable.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Banks are not a safe haven in a bust: high rates lift their earnings, but the multiple awarded can roughly halve, so a 30% earnings gain still leaves the share price lower overall.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In a bust cycle high return-on-capital companies still tend to go flat or mildly negative over two to three years, but they lose much less value than the market, so the analyst keeps part of the portfolio in them.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst allocates to whichever asset class offers the best prospective return at the time, which in a bust can mean a 10% fixed-income return being the best available option because the alternative is negative.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's circular debt comes in two distinct forms: the power-sector plan that has been negotiated with banks, and a separate gas-sector receivable which is what actually owes money to the exploration companies.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Power-sector circular debt accrues late-payment interest under government contracts, whereas the gas-sector receivables owed to exploration companies do not, which removes the urgency to retire them because the amount is not compounding.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A power-sector circular debt resolution does not help the gas exploration companies; a dedicated gas circular debt retirement plan would be a large benefit for them, and the analyst is genuinely unsure one will materialise.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When the government previously settled part of this company's gas receivable, very little interest was paid on the overdue amount, reinforcing that gas arrears carry no meaningful carrying cost for the payer.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Essential medicines receive an annual price adjustment equal to about 70% of the CPI inflation rate, so roughly 4-5% inflation translates into a permitted increase of about 3%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pharmaceutical pricing carries heavy operating leverage: with other costs unchanged, a 3% price increase lifts profit roughly 10-12%, and a 5% increase can lift it about 15%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Not every medicine captures the full allowed annual increase, because some are already priced below their approved maximum while others were raised by more than the permitted percentage in an earlier year.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Active pharmaceutical ingredient costs are the other half of pharma margins and paracetamol's input is strongly linked to the oil price, so earnings can rise on falling API costs even without a price increase.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: An in-housing and expansion project is due to come online in 2026 and is expected to generate around 2 billion rupees of annual savings, which is not reflected in the company's current earnings per share.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst values the company either by adding the future expansion saving to current earnings and applying about 15 times, or by applying roughly 20 times to current earnings, to avoid double counting.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst rates the consumer-health business among Pakistan's finest for its brand equity, which lets it keep raising prices after deregulation, while its scale means quarter-on-quarter growth cannot stay exceptional.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Fertilizer production runs level through the year while sales are weak in the first two quarters and strong in the last two; unsold output sits in closing inventory, so reported cost tracks sales and quarterly margins are not distorted.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst treats the electric-vehicle venture as a small part of the company: even on a generous valuation it would be a minority of total value, with the bulk still sitting in power plants and other projects.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The company now owns only half of the electric-vehicle venture, the rest sitting with a private holding, so listed shareholders capture just 50% of whatever value it creates, on top of an already high base valuation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: An exciting new venture only moves a share price if it is large relative to the parent: the analyst sizes the venture's plausible future value, applies the parent's ownership share, and compares that with the parent's existing value.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: If the electric-vehicle policy is approved with strong tax incentives, EV prices could become the best in their category and a Chinese entrant could plausibly become Pakistan's leading car brand.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The tractor maker has an excellent long-run return record, but the analyst says an investment case still requires a view on when tractor sales recover and on profit per tractor.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst cites the IT firm as a business whose existing operations keep growing with improving returns on capital and a strengthening foothold in Europe and the United States, rather than needing a new venture to rerate.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistani IT services compete on human capital rather than infrastructure, and the country's lower salary levels by global standards are the structural advantage behind the sector's export growth.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Sector-level analytical templates do not transfer within Pakistani IT because each company's business model differs, unlike banking or cement where one framework applies to ten or twenty names.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The media company is an asset-light, high return-on-capital business: it owns no distinctive buildings or assets, and its value comes from creating entertainment that attracts advertising.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst notes the share trades on a low single-digit earnings multiple while intrinsic value compounds roughly 25-30% a year, so a flat price mechanically compresses the multiple further each year until it reprices.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A sports venture briefly pushed results to break-even because advance payments were made to well-known cricketers for tournament broadcast rights, a cost the analyst regards as having since normalised.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst keeps the position small because the timing of value realisation is unknowable: the share can sit still for long stretches and then adjust abruptly through a run of upper locks.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst works from the principle that time is a friend of a good business: a high return-on-capital company compounds value as years pass, so it needs no new venture to be a sound investment.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Gold-mining announcements by fertilizer and cement companies rest on reserve confirmation without a completed feasibility study, and the analyst sees cash inflows only three to four years out, making immediate valuation premature.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because the market prices projects two to three years ahead, the analyst only invests in a long-dated venture when he can both understand its economics and still buy at an attractive price.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Portfolio size and market liquidity dictate strategy: a small fund can take advantage of deeply undervalued small positions, while a fund many times larger must assume a holding cannot be exited for years and so screens differently.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst warns that one month or even one year of outperformance has very low predictive value for the next period, so selecting a manager on recent numbers alone is unreliable.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Boom and bust cycles are not peculiar to Pakistan: frontier and emerging markets see long, deep declines, and even the US market's price-earnings multiple oscillates roughly between 8 and 25 times.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst expects to be in a minority when calling the turn of a boom cycle, because at that moment the loudest consensus is that further large gains remain; the decision must rest on tracked facts, not opinion.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Options in a bust differ by investor location: overseas holders can move into foreign currency, gold or global markets directly, while domestic investors are largely limited to Shariah-compliant fixed income or physical gold.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst finds no long-run return penalty from Shariah-compliant investing in Pakistan: the compliant and conventional universes alternate in leadership year to year and most of the long-run multibaggers he studies are compliant.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ARN AGM 2025' (YouTube transcript, undated)
